primary_claim: R²-dLLM reduces decoding steps by up to 88% versus existing decoding strategies while maintaining competitive generation quality.
Adaptive steering improves the control-quality balance over uniform and interval-restricted baselines across seven tasks and four DLMs.
Saber improves code generation Pass@1 by an average of 1.9% over mainstream DLM samplers while achieving an average 251.4% inference speedup.
SSD achieves up to 3.46× speedup while producing outputs identical to stepwise decoding.
SlowFast Sampling achieves up to 15.63× speedup on LLaDA with minimal accuracy drop, and up to 34.22× with caching.
DBLast improves accepted draft length over independent block sampling, especially in higher-entropy decoding regimes.
RPS achieves 4–10× wall-clock speedup over the standard decoder while preserving generation quality.
dKV-Cache achieves 2–10× inference speedup for diffusion language models, narrowing their speed gap with autoregressive models.
mec_evidence: Tables 1–3 report quality and speedups, but no measured wall-clock time, author-timed baseline, or named hardware for the headline comparison.

primary_claim: DyStruct significantly improves generation quality and flexibility over fixed-length and flexible-length diffusion baselines.
Conv decoding and R2FT achieve state-of-the-art open-ended generation results among diffusion language models with lower step size, improving speed and quality.
ETE reduces decoding rounds compared with confidence-only baselines while maintaining generation quality.
Activation steering produces large behavioral shifts and is substantially more effective than prompt-based and optimization-based baselines.
Our protein co-design approach achieves state-of-the-art performance while supporting flexible generation of sequence or structure with one multimodal model.
LLaDA-MoE achieves state-of-the-art performance among diffusion language models with larger parameters across multiple benchmarks.
RCD nearly doubles baseline accuracy on AIME tasks while requiring up to 4–5× fewer denoising steps at baseline peak accuracy.
ILMs outperform autoregressive and masked diffusion models on planning tasks, and outperform MDMs while matching ARMs on unconditional text generation.
Joint AR and diffusion objectives complement each other: diffusion improves lookahead planning, while AR provides left-to-right linguistic priors.
MGDM achieves higher accuracy than autoregressive models on complex tasks, including 91.5% on Countdown and 100% on Sudoku versus 45.8% and 20.7%.
NAP achieves stronger math benchmark performance under parallel decoding than DLMs trained on standard long-CoT data, with gains increasing at higher parallelism.
BDLM Mamba-H achieves higher long-context inference throughput than full-sequence DiffuMamba-H and BDLM attention at specified context lengths.
SPREAD significantly improves answer precision and mitigates Response Semantic Drift in retrieval-augmented diffusion language models.
DLMs encode denoising progress in residual streams, and steering its inferred subspace predictably modulates confidence and entropy.
TAD improves the accuracy-parallelism trade-off, raising LLaDA average accuracy from 46.2% to 51.6% and average AUP from 46.2 to 257.1.
TraDo-8B-Instruct improves mathematical reasoning accuracy by 6.1% over Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and 51.3% over Llama3.1-8B-Instruct.
PAPO outperforms baselines, gaining 4.5% on GSM8K, 4.8% on MATH500, 42.2% on Countdown, and 16.1% on Sudoku.
CAPR achieves state-of-the-art RL-tuned dLLM results at 256- and 512-token budgets and matches the strongest tree baseline on Sudoku at under one third the per-step compute.
AGRPO achieves accuracy gains of 59.4% on Countdown and 69.7% on Sudoku over base LLaDA, exceeding diffu-GRPO.
TRIMS improves the accuracy-parallelism trade-off over standard MDLM training and train-free acceleration baselines.
DLLM-TTS enables efficient speech synthesis through parallel generation within blocks, reporting a real-time factor of 0.15.
ECF improves answer accuracy by 2.62 percentage points on average over the strongest fixed top-k input across five visual QA benchmarks.
Shortening the KV-cache refresh interval yields a monotonic speed–agreement frontier and near-exact baseline agreement at a measured 1.3× speedup.
FUDOKI achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art autoregressive MLLMs across visual understanding and image generation tasks.
MMaDA-8B surpasses named baselines in textual reasoning, multimodal understanding, and text-to-image generation.
dVLA achieves a 96.4% average success rate on LIBERO, surpassing discrete and continuous action policies.
Meta-DiffuB achieves state-of-the-art performance against prior S2S diffusion models and fine-tuned language models across four Seq2Seq benchmarks.
SLD achieves competitive or superior fluency, coherence, and contextual compatibility versus diffusion and autoregressive baselines.
TextLDM matches GPT-2 under the same settings and substantially outperforms prior diffusion language models.
AURORA-LM achieves the strongest performance among evaluated continuous and diffusion-based language models on OpenWebText free generation and XSum summarization.
DiffS2UT achieves comparable translation results to autoregressive baselines with significantly fewer decoding steps.
PoetryDiffusion outperforms existing models on automatic semantic, metrical, and overall metrics and human evaluation across two poetry datasets.
